name: Information Security Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal information security policy governing the protection of systems, data, and operational resilience. Effective from 2026-01-15, owned by the Chief Information Security Officer and applicable to all staff, technology, risk, and board audiences. The policy is mandated by FCA COBS Part 5 and PRA Operational Resilience requirements.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 5, PRA Operational Resilience

name: FCA COBS Part 5
description: Financial Conduct Authority regulation on conduct of business rules, Part 5, which mandates information security and operational resilience requirements for FirstUK Bank.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 5, PRA Operational Resilience

name: PRA Operational Resilience
description: Prudential Regulation Authority regulatory framework requiring operational resilience standards, including information security and business continuity measures applicable to FirstUK Bank.
context: Regulatory Reference | FCA COBS Part 5, PRA Operational Resilience

name: Chief Information Security Officer
description: Executive role responsible for ownership and governance of the Information Security Policy at FirstUK Bank. Accountable for policy development, implementation, and oversight across all staff and technology functions.

name: All Staff
description: Collective responsibility of all FirstUK Bank employees to comply with information security policy requirements and maintain operational security standards.
context: Audience | All Staff, Technology, Risk, Board

name: Technology Department
description: Department responsible for implementing and maintaining information security controls, systems, and technical safeguards under the policy.
context: Audience | All Staff, Technology, Risk, Board

name: Risk Function
description: Risk management function responsible for oversight, monitoring, and governance of information security risks and compliance with the policy.
context: Audience | All Staff, Technology, Risk, Board

name: Board
description: Board-level governance body with accountability for information security policy oversight and strategic direction.
context: Audience | All Staff, Technology, Risk, Board

name: Information Security Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's formal policy governing the protection of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer data, systems, and intellectual property. The policy is designed to mitigate threats including cyberattacks, unauthorized access, and data breaches.
context: FirstUK Bank maintains an Information Security Policy to protect confidentiality, integrity, and availability of customer data, systems, and intellectual property against threats (cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data breaches).

name: Cyberattack
description: A threat to the bank's systems and data through malicious digital attacks. This is identified as a key risk that the Information Security Policy is designed to address.
context: against threats (cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data breaches)

name: Unauthorized Access
description: The risk of individuals gaining access to customer data, systems, or intellectual property without proper authorization. This is a primary threat the policy seeks to prevent.
context: against threats (cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data breaches)

name: Data Breach
description: The unauthorized disclosure or loss of customer data or intellectual property. This is identified as a key threat that the Information Security Policy is designed to mitigate.
context: against threats (cyberattacks, unauthorized access, data breaches)

name: Information Security Policy
description: A formal policy establishing security procedures to prevent unauthorized access to systems and data, protect customer data against breaches, ensure system availability and reliability, respond rapidly to security incidents, and meet regulatory security standards set by the PRA and FCA.
context: To establish security procedures that: Prevent unauthorized access to systems/data
Meet regulatory security standards (PRA Operational Resilience, FCA)

name: Prudential Regulation Authority
description: UK regulatory authority that sets operational resilience standards which this security policy must comply with.
context: Meet regulatory security standards (PRA Operational Resilience, FCA)

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: UK regulatory authority that sets security standards which this policy must comply with.
context: Meet regulatory security standards (PRA Operational Resilience, FCA)

name: PRA Operational Resilience Standard
description: Regulatory standard issued by the PRA requiring firms to maintain operational resilience and security controls.
context: Meet regulatory security standards (PRA Operational Resilience, FCA)

name: Unauthorized Access
description: The risk of unauthorized parties gaining access to banking systems or data, which the policy is designed to prevent through security procedures.

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of customer data being compromised or exposed, which the policy addresses through protective measures.

name: System Unavailability
description: The risk of systems becoming unavailable or unreliable, which the policy mitigates through availability and reliability controls.

name: Security Incident
description: A security event or breach requiring rapid response and investigation, which the policy establishes procedures to address.

name: Prevent Unauthorized Access to Systems and Data
description: A core requirement to implement security procedures that prevent unauthorized parties from accessing banking systems or customer data.

name: Protect Customer Data Against Breaches
description: A requirement to implement protective measures and safeguards to ensure customer data is protected against security breaches.

name: Ensure System Availability and Reliability
description: A requirement to maintain systems in a state of continuous availability and reliable operation to support banking services.

name: Rapid Response to Security Incidents
description: A requirement to establish and execute rapid response procedures when security incidents occur.

name: Compliance with Regulatory Security Standards
description: A requirement to meet and maintain compliance with security standards set by the PRA and FCA.
context: Meet regulatory security standards (PRA Operational Resilience, FCA)

name: Data Protection and Privacy Policy
description: A comprehensive policy governing the protection and handling of all customer data, including personal and financial information, across all systems, infrastructure, staff, contractors, third parties, and physical and digital assets across all geographic locations.
context: Applies to: All customer data (personal, financial)

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorized access to or compromise of customer personal and financial data held across all systems and infrastructure.

name: Unauthorized Access
description: The risk of unauthorized access to customer data and organizational assets by staff, contractors, third parties, or external actors across physical and digital environments.

name: All Staff
description: All organizational staff members are subject to data protection obligations under this policy, including compliance with requirements for handling customer data and protecting organizational assets.

name: Contractors
description: Contractors engaged by the organization are subject to data protection obligations and must comply with requirements for handling customer data and protecting organizational assets.

name: Third Parties
description: Third parties engaged or working with the organization are subject to data protection obligations and must comply with requirements for handling customer data and protecting organizational assets.

name: Data Access Control
description: Control measures governing access to customer data and organizational assets across all systems and infrastructure to prevent unauthorized access.

name: Data Encryption
description: Technical safeguards for encrypting customer personal and financial data across all systems and infrastructure.

name: Information Security Policy
description: FirstUK Bank's overarching policy mandating the protection of customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls, incident response procedures, and continuous threat monitoring. The policy establishes the bank's commitment to multi-layered security safeguards and proactive threat detection.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls, incident response, and continuous threat monitoring.

name: Data Breach
description: The risk of unauthorized access to or compromise of customer data held by FirstUK Bank. This risk category encompasses threats to the confidentiality and integrity of sensitive customer information.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls

name: Information Security Risk
description: The risk of compromise, disruption, or unauthorized access to FirstUK Bank's systems and infrastructure. This encompasses threats to system availability, integrity, and confidentiality.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls, incident response, and continuous threat monitoring.

name: Defense-in-Depth Security Controls
description: A multi-layered security control framework implemented by FirstUK Bank to protect customer data and systems. The defense-in-depth approach employs multiple independent security mechanisms to ensure that compromise of one layer does not result in total system failure.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls

name: Incident Response
description: The operational procedures and protocols established by FirstUK Bank to detect, respond to, and manage security incidents affecting customer data and systems. This control measure is a core component of the bank's information security framework.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls, incident response, and continuous threat monitoring.

name: Continuous Threat Monitoring
description: A continuous monitoring mechanism implemented by FirstUK Bank to detect and identify security threats to customer data and systems. This proactive control measure enables early detection and response to emerging threats.
context: FirstUK Bank protects customer data and systems through defense-in-depth security controls, incident response, and continuous threat monitoring.

name: Information Security Policy
description: A foundational information security policy establishing three core security principles: Zero-Trust Security (continuous verification with no implicit trust), Defense-in-Depth (multiple layered controls), and the CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability). The policy mandates proactive breach assumption and comprehensive protective measures across network, system, data, and process layers.
context: Zero-Trust Security: No implicit trust (users, devices, networks)
Defense-in-Depth: Multiple layers of security controls

name: Zero-Trust Authentication and Authorization Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement that all access requests must be subject to continuous authentication and authorization with no implicit trust granted to users, devices, or networks. Every access request must be verified independently.

name: Proactive Breach Defense Obligation
description: Mandatory obligation to assume breach conditions and implement proactive defensive measures. Staff and systems must operate under the assumption that a breach may occur and design controls accordingly.

name: Multi-Layer Security Control Implementation
description: Mandatory requirement to implement multiple layers of security controls across network, system, data, and process domains to eliminate single points of failure and ensure defense-in-depth.

name: Data Confidentiality Through Encryption and Access Control
description: Mandatory requirement to protect data confidentiality through encryption and access control mechanisms, ensuring that sensitive data is protected from unauthorized disclosure.

name: Data Integrity Protection Against Unauthorized Modification
description: Mandatory requirement to ensure data integrity by preventing unauthorized modification of data. Controls must guarantee that data cannot be altered without proper authorization.
context: Integrity: Data cannot be modified without authorization

name: System Availability Assurance
description: Mandatory requirement to maintain system availability and ensure that critical systems and data remain accessible to authorized users when needed for business operations.

name: Unauthorized Access
description: Risk of unauthorized users, devices, or networks gaining access to systems or data. Addressed through zero-trust security principles requiring continuous authentication and authorization.

name: Data Breach
description: Risk of data confidentiality compromise through unauthorized disclosure or access. Mitigated through encryption, access controls, and defense-in-depth layered protections.

name: Data Integrity Compromise
description: Risk of unauthorized modification or corruption of data. Addressed through integrity controls that prevent data alteration without proper authorization.
context: Data cannot be modified without authorization

name: System Unavailability
description: Risk of systems or data becoming inaccessible when needed for business operations. Mitigated through availability controls and defense-in-depth architecture with no single points of failure.

name: Continuous Authentication and Authorization
description: Operational control requiring continuous verification of every access request with no implicit trust. Implements zero-trust security by verifying users, devices, and networks on every access attempt.

name: Multi-Layer Security Control Architecture
description: Operational safeguard implementing defense-in-depth through multiple layers of security controls across network, system, data, and process domains to eliminate single points of failure.

name: Data Encryption
description: Technical control protecting data confidentiality through encryption mechanisms, ensuring that sensitive data is protected from unauthorized disclosure.

name: Access Control Mechanism
description: Operational control limiting access to data and systems based on authorization rules, supporting both confidentiality and integrity objectives.

name: Data Integrity Verification
description: Control mechanism ensuring that data cannot be modified without authorization, protecting data integrity through verification and authorization requirements.
context: Data cannot be modified without authorization

name: Ransomware
description: A cyberattack threat that FirstUK Bank monitors as part of its threat landscape. Ransomware represents a malicious software attack designed to encrypt or disable critical systems and data.

name: Malware
description: A cyberattack threat monitored by FirstUK Bank involving malicious software designed to compromise systems, steal data, or disrupt operations.

name: Phishing
description: A cyberattack threat monitored by FirstUK Bank involving deceptive communications designed to trick users into revealing sensitive information or credentials.

name: Unauthorized Access
description: A threat category monitored by FirstUK Bank encompassing hacking, credential theft, and social engineering attacks that enable attackers to gain illicit access to systems or accounts.
context: Unauthorized Access: Hacking, credential theft, social engineering

name: Hacking
description: A threat involving unauthorized access to systems or accounts through technical exploitation, monitored as part of FirstUK Bank's unauthorized access threat category.
context: Unauthorized Access: Hacking, credential theft, social engineering

name: Credential Theft
description: A threat involving the theft of user credentials or authentication information, monitored by FirstUK Bank as a component of unauthorized access risks.
context: Unauthorized Access: Hacking, credential theft, social engineering

name: Social Engineering
description: A threat involving manipulation of individuals to divulge confidential information or perform actions that compromise security, monitored by FirstUK Bank as an unauthorized access risk.
context: Unauthorized Access: Hacking, credential theft, social engineering

name: Data Breach
description: A threat involving the theft or exposure of sensitive data, monitored by FirstUK Bank as a critical information security risk.
context: Data Breaches: Sensitive data theft, exposure

name: Insider Threat
description: A threat originating from within the organization, including disgruntled staff and inadvertent disclosure of sensitive information, monitored by FirstUK Bank.
context: Insider Threats: Disgruntled staff, inadvertent disclosure

name: Third-Party Risk
description: A threat arising from vendor compromise or supply chain attacks that could impact FirstUK Bank's operations and security, monitored as part of the threat landscape.
context: Third-Party Risk: Vendor compromise, supply chain attacks

name: Natural Disaster
description: A threat category encompassing power outages, fire, and flooding that could disrupt FirstUK Bank's operations and infrastructure, monitored as part of the threat landscape.
context: Natural Disasters: Power outages, fire, flooding

name: Access Control Policy
description: Policy governing authentication and access control mechanisms for both customers and staff across online banking, mobile applications, branch operations, and remote access. Establishes multi-factor authentication requirements and physical security controls.

name: Customer Online Banking Authentication Requirement
description: Mandates that customers accessing online banking must authenticate using username/password combined with one-time password delivered via email or SMS.

name: Customer Mobile App Authentication Requirement
description: Requires customers using the mobile app to authenticate via biometric methods (fingerprint or facial recognition) with optional PIN as secondary factor.

name: Customer Branch Authentication Requirement
description: Mandates photo identification verification for customers accessing services at branch locations.

name: Staff Directory Authentication Requirement
description: Requires all staff to authenticate using LDAP/Active Directory credentials with username and password for system access.

name: Privileged Staff Multi-Factor Authentication Requirement
description: Mandates multi-factor authentication for staff with privileged access roles including administrative and compliance functions.

name: Staff Physical Badge Access Requirement
description: Requires staff to use physical badges for facility access control.

name: Remote Staff VPN Access Requirement
description: Mandates that staff accessing systems remotely must use a virtual private network (VPN) connection.

name: One-Time Password Authentication
description: Technical control implementing one-time password delivery via email or SMS for customer online banking authentication.

name: Biometric Authentication
description: Technical control implementing fingerprint and facial recognition authentication for mobile app access.

name: LDAP/Active Directory Authentication
description: Directory-based authentication system for staff system access using centralized username and password credentials.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication for Privileged Access
description: Technical control requiring multiple authentication factors for staff with administrative and compliance privileges.

name: Physical Badge Access Control
description: Physical security control using badge-based access to restrict facility entry to authorized staff.

name: Virtual Private Network Access
description: Network security control requiring encrypted VPN connection for remote staff access to systems.

name: Customer
description: End users accessing banking services through online banking, mobile applications, or branch channels, subject to authentication requirements.

name: Staff
description: Bank employees required to authenticate using directory credentials and comply with multi-factor authentication for privileged roles.

name: Privileged Staff
description: Staff members with administrative or compliance access roles subject to enhanced multi-factor authentication requirements.

name: Remote Staff
description: Staff members accessing bank systems from locations outside the physical facility, required to use VPN.

name: Role-Based Access Control Policy
description: Policy governing role-based access control and authorization across the bank, defining which staff roles can access specific data and systems. Establishes segregation of duties to prevent conflicts of interest and requires comprehensive audit logging of all access events.
context: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Customer-facing staff: Limited customer data (own customers)
Compliance staff: Full data access + audit logging
Technology staff: System access with audit trail

name: Customer-Facing Staff Data Access Limitation
description: Requires customer-facing staff to access only limited customer data restricted to their own customers, preventing unauthorized access to other customer information.
context: Customer-facing staff: Limited customer data (own customers)

name: Compliance Staff Full Data Access with Audit Logging
description: Grants compliance staff full data access across the bank with mandatory audit logging of all access events for accountability and monitoring purposes.
context: Compliance staff: Full data access + audit logging

name: Technology Staff System Access with Audit Trail
description: Permits technology staff to access systems with all actions recorded in an audit trail for security and accountability purposes.
context: Technology staff: System access with audit trail

name: Executive Access to Aggregated Reports Only
description: Restricts executive access to aggregated reports only, preventing direct access to granular customer or transaction data.

name: Developer Access to Pre-Production Environments Only
description: Limits developer access to pre-production environments only, preventing direct access to production systems and live customer data.

name: Segregation of Account Opening and Approval
description: Prohibits the same individual from both initiating and approving account opening, ensuring independent review and preventing unauthorized account creation.

name: Segregation of Transaction Initiation and Approval
description: Prohibits the same individual from both initiating and approving transactions, ensuring dual control over financial movements.

name: Segregation of System Administration and Application Development
description: Prohibits the same individual from performing both system administration and application development, preventing unauthorized system modifications.

name: Segregation of Audit and Tested System Ownership
description: Prohibits the same individual from conducting audits of systems they own or have tested, ensuring independent audit verification.

name: Comprehensive Access Logging Requirement
description: Mandates logging of all access events including who accessed what, when, and from where, creating an audit trail for all system and data access.
context: All access logged (who, what, when, where)

name: Audit Log Retention Period
description: Requires retention of audit logs for a minimum of one year to support compliance investigations and historical access reviews.

name: Suspicious Access Pattern Flagging
description: Requires identification and flagging of suspicious access patterns to detect potential unauthorized access attempts or policy violations.

name: Periodic Access Review
description: Mandates quarterly reviews of user access rights to ensure continued appropriateness and identify obsolete or excessive permissions.

name: Access Logging System
description: Technical control that records all access events including user identity, data accessed, timestamp, and location to create a comprehensive audit trail.
context: All access logged (who, what, when, where)

name: Suspicious Access Pattern Detection
description: Monitoring mechanism that identifies and flags unusual access patterns that may indicate unauthorized access attempts or policy violations.

name: Quarterly Access Review Process
description: Periodic control procedure that reviews user access rights on a quarterly basis to ensure continued appropriateness and compliance with segregation of duties.

name: Customer-Facing Staff
description: Staff members with direct customer interaction responsibilities, restricted to accessing limited customer data for their own customers only.
context: Customer-facing staff: Limited customer data (own customers)

name: Compliance Staff
description: Compliance personnel granted full data access across the bank with all access events subject to audit logging for regulatory oversight.
context: Compliance staff: Full data access + audit logging

name: Technology Staff
description: Technical personnel with system access rights, with all actions recorded in an audit trail for security accountability.
context: Technology staff: System access with audit trail

name: Executives
description: Senior management personnel restricted to access of aggregated reports only, preventing direct access to granular data.

name: Developers
description: Software development personnel restricted to pre-production environments only, preventing access to production systems and live data.

name: Data Encryption Policy
description: Policy governing encryption of data in transit across internet-facing connections and remote access channels. Establishes mandatory use of TLS 1.3 for all internet connections, HTTPS enforcement, mTLS for internal service communication, and VPN requirements for remote staff access with multi-factor authentication.

name: TLS 1.3 Encryption for Internet-Facing Connections
description: Mandatory requirement that all internet-facing connections must be encrypted using TLS 1.3 (Transport Layer Security). Includes certificate management with auto-renewal and monitoring capabilities.
context: TLS 1.3 (Transport Layer Security): All internet-facing connections encrypted

name: HTTPS Enforcement with HTTP Redirect
description: Mandatory requirement to enforce HTTPS protocol for all web connections, with automatic redirection of HTTP traffic to HTTPS to prevent unencrypted data transmission.

name: Mutual TLS for Internal Service Communication
description: Mandatory requirement for mutual TLS (mTLS) encryption on all internal service-to-service communication to ensure bidirectional authentication and encryption of internal traffic.

name: VPN Requirement for Remote Staff Access
description: Mandatory requirement that all staff working remotely must use VPN to encrypt all traffic through a secure tunnel, protecting data in transit from remote locations.
context: All traffic encrypted through secure tunnel

name: Multi-Factor Authentication for Remote Access
description: Mandatory requirement that multi-factor authentication must be required for all remote staff accessing the bank's systems via VPN.

name: TLS 1.3 Encryption Implementation
description: Technical control implementing TLS 1.3 encryption for all internet-facing connections with automated certificate management including renewal and monitoring.
context: TLS 1.3 (Transport Layer Security): All internet-facing connections encrypted

name: HTTPS Enforcement Control
description: Technical control that enforces HTTPS protocol and automatically redirects unencrypted HTTP traffic to HTTPS endpoints.

name: Mutual TLS Authentication Control
description: Technical control implementing mutual TLS for internal service-to-service communication, ensuring bidirectional certificate-based authentication and encryption.

name: VPN Encryption Tunnel
description: Technical control providing encrypted VPN tunnel for remote staff to securely transmit all traffic to the bank's network.
context: All traffic encrypted through secure tunnel

name: Multi-Factor Authentication for Remote Access
description: Access control requiring multi-factor authentication as a prerequisite for remote staff to establish VPN connections.

name: Remote Staff
description: Staff members working remotely who are required to use VPN with multi-factor authentication to encrypt all traffic and maintain secure access to bank systems.

name: Data Breach in Transit
description: Risk of unauthorized interception or exposure of sensitive data transmitted over internet-facing connections or remote access channels due to lack of encryption.
context: All traffic encrypted through secure tunnel

name: Unauthorized Internal Service Access
description: Risk of unauthorized access to internal service-to-service communications due to lack of mutual authentication and encryption.

name: Remote Access Compromise
description: Risk of unauthorized access to bank systems by remote staff or interception of remote traffic due to lack of encryption or weak authentication.

name: Data Encryption at Rest Policy
description: Policy governing encryption of sensitive data while stored in databases, backups, and file systems. Establishes standards for encryption algorithms, key management, and secure deletion procedures across on-premises and cloud environments.

name: Database Sensitive Column Encryption Requirement
description: Mandates AES-256 encryption for all sensitive columns stored in databases, with encryption keys maintained separately in Hardware Security Modules to prevent unauthorized access.

name: Transparent Application-Level Encryption Implementation
description: Requires transparent encryption at the application level to ensure sensitive data is encrypted without requiring changes to application code or user workflows.

name: Backup Encryption Standard
description: Mandates AES-256 encryption for all backups stored to S3, with encryption keys managed through AWS KMS and tested recovery procedures to ensure data integrity.

name: File Storage Encryption Across Environments
description: Requires encryption of file storage in both on-premises and cloud environments, including encrypted USB and portable devices to protect data in transit and at rest.

name: Secure Data Deletion Procedure
description: Mandates secure overwriting of deleted data using Department of Defense standards to ensure sensitive information cannot be recovered from storage media.

name: AES-256 Database Encryption
description: Cryptographic control implementing AES-256 encryption algorithm for sensitive database columns to protect data confidentiality at rest.

name: Hardware Security Module Key Storage
description: Secure key management control that stores encryption keys separately in Hardware Security Modules, preventing unauthorized access to encryption keys.

name: AWS KMS Backup Key Management
description: Cloud-based key management service that manages encryption keys for S3 backups, providing centralized control and audit logging of key access.

name: Backup Recovery Testing Procedure
description: Operational control requiring regular testing of backup recovery procedures to verify encrypted backups can be successfully restored and remain accessible.

name: Secure Data Overwriting Control
description: Technical control implementing Department of Defense standard secure overwriting procedures to ensure deleted data cannot be recovered from storage media.

name: Unauthorized Data Access
description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive data stored in databases, backups, or file systems due to inadequate encryption or key management controls.

name: Data Recovery Failure
description: Risk of inability to recover encrypted backups due to key loss, corruption, or untested recovery procedures, resulting in data loss.

name: Data Residue After Deletion
description: Risk of sensitive data remaining recoverable from storage media after deletion due to inadequate overwriting procedures.

name: Network Security Policy
description: Policy governing network security controls including firewall configuration, DDoS protection, and intrusion detection/prevention mechanisms. Establishes requirements for perimeter security, traffic monitoring, and automated threat response.

name: Stateful Firewall Inspection Requirement
description: Requirement to implement stateful inspection firewall as the primary perimeter security control. Firewall must restrict ingress to HTTPS (Port 443) only for public APIs and enforce whitelist-based egress restrictions.
context: Ingress: Port 443 (HTTPS) only for public APIs

name: Firewall Rule Logging and Monitoring Obligation
description: Requirement to log and monitor all firewall rules to maintain audit trail and detect policy violations or suspicious patterns.

name: DDoS Protection Implementation Requirement
description: Requirement to implement managed DDoS protection using AWS Shield, rate limiting on APIs, anomalous traffic detection, and automated traffic rerouting in response to detected DDoS attacks.

name: Intrusion Detection and Prevention System Deployment
description: Requirement to deploy both network-based and host-based intrusion detection systems with automated response capabilities to block malicious IP addresses.

name: Stateful Inspection Firewall
description: Perimeter security control implementing stateful packet inspection with port-based ingress restrictions (HTTPS only) and whitelist-based egress filtering. All firewall rules are logged and monitored.
context: Ingress: Port 443 (HTTPS) only for public APIs

name: AWS Shield DDoS Protection
description: Managed DDoS protection service providing rate limiting on APIs, anomalous traffic detection, and automated traffic rerouting to mitigate distributed denial-of-service attacks.

name: Network-Based Intrusion Detection System
description: Network-based intrusion detection system using Snort-like rules to identify and alert on suspicious network traffic patterns and potential attacks.

name: Host-Based Intrusion Detection System
description: Host-based intrusion detection system deployed on critical systems to monitor system-level activities and detect unauthorized access or malicious behavior.

name: Automated Malicious IP Blocking
description: Automated response mechanism that blocks malicious IP addresses detected by intrusion detection systems to prevent ongoing attacks.

name: Distributed Denial of Service Attack
description: Risk of service disruption through coordinated high-volume traffic attacks targeting network infrastructure and APIs. Mitigated through rate limiting, traffic detection, and rerouting mechanisms.

name: Unauthorized Network Access
description: Risk of unauthorized access to network resources and critical systems through exploitation of vulnerabilities or malicious network activity. Addressed through firewall controls, intrusion detection, and automated blocking.

name: Internal Network Segmentation Policy
description: Policy governing the segregation and isolation of internal banking networks to protect customer-facing systems, staff systems, databases, and development environments from unauthorized access and cross-system compromise.

name: Customer-Facing Systems Network Isolation
description: Requirement that customer-facing systems must operate on a separate subnet from other internal systems to prevent unauthorized access and maintain system integrity.

name: Internal Staff Systems Network Isolation
description: Requirement that internal staff systems must operate on a separate subnet from customer-facing systems and other critical infrastructure.

name: Database Tier Isolation and Access Restriction
description: Requirement that the database tier must be isolated from other network segments with restricted access controls to prevent unauthorized data access.

name: Development Systems Separation from Production
description: Requirement that development systems must be segregated from production systems to prevent untested code or configurations from affecting live customer services.

name: Remote Access via VPN Only
description: Requirement that all remote access to internal systems must be conducted exclusively through a Virtual Private Network to ensure encrypted and authenticated connections.

name: Bastion Host for Administrative Access
description: Requirement that administrative access to internal systems must be routed through a bastion host to provide a controlled gateway and audit point for privileged operations.

name: Multi-Hop Authentication for Remote Access
description: Requirement that remote access authentication must employ multi-hop authentication mechanisms to strengthen identity verification and prevent unauthorized access.

name: Session Logging and Timeout for Remote Access
description: Requirement that all remote access sessions must be logged for audit purposes and configured with automatic timeout to prevent unauthorized prolonged access.

name: Network Subnet Segregation
description: Technical control implementing the separation of customer-facing systems, internal staff systems, database tier, and development systems into isolated network subnets to prevent unauthorized cross-system access.

name: VPN Remote Access Gateway
description: Technical control requiring all remote access to internal systems to be encrypted and authenticated through a Virtual Private Network gateway.

name: Bastion Host Access Control
description: Technical control implementing a hardened gateway server through which all administrative access to internal systems must be routed, providing centralized authentication and audit logging.

name: Multi-Hop Authentication
description: Technical control requiring multiple sequential authentication steps for remote access to strengthen identity verification and prevent unauthorized access.

name: Session Logging and Audit Trail
description: Technical control that records all remote access sessions for audit and forensic purposes, enabling detection and investigation of unauthorized access attempts.

name: Session Timeout Mechanism
description: Technical control that automatically terminates idle remote access sessions after a defined period to prevent unauthorized use of abandoned connections.

name: Unauthorized Network Access
description: Risk that attackers or unauthorized internal users could gain access to customer-facing systems, staff systems, or databases through inadequate network segregation.

name: Cross-System Compromise
description: Risk that a compromise of one network segment could spread to other critical systems if development, production, customer-facing, and internal systems are not properly segregated.

name: Unauthorized Remote Access
description: Risk that remote users could gain unauthorized access to internal systems through unencrypted connections or weak authentication mechanisms.

name: Privileged Access Abuse
description: Risk that administrative users could abuse their elevated privileges to access unauthorized systems or data without detection.

name: Endpoint Security Policy
description: A comprehensive information security policy governing the deployment, configuration, and management of endpoint protection controls across laptops, desktops, and mobile devices. The policy mandates antivirus/anti-malware deployment, device encryption, patch management, and remote wipe capabilities to protect systems and customer data.
context: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tool deployed
Mandatory for all devices with customer data access

name: Endpoint Detection and Response Tool Deployment
description: Requires deployment of an Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) tool across all endpoints with real-time scanning enabled and automatic isolation of suspicious behavior.
context: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tool deployed

name: Virus Definition Update Requirement
description: Mandates that virus definitions be updated daily to ensure current protection against known malware threats.

name: Device Encryption Enforcement
description: Requires encryption to be enforced on all devices, particularly those with access to customer data. Specifies BitLocker for Windows and FileVault for Mac with mandatory key escrow for recovery purposes.
context: Mandatory for all devices with customer data access

name: Operating System Patch Application Schedule
description: Establishes a tiered patch management schedule requiring standard OS patches to be applied within 30 days and critical patches within 7 days.
context: OS patches applied within 30 days (critical within 7)

name: Mobile Device Management Implementation
description: Requires Mobile Device Management (MDM) to be implemented for all phones and tablets to enable centralized device control and security management.

name: Lost Device Remote Wipe Capability
description: Mandates that all managed devices have the capability to be remotely wiped if lost or stolen to prevent unauthorized access to customer data.

name: Encryption Key Escrow and Recovery
description: Requires that encryption keys be escrowed to enable recovery of encrypted data when necessary, supporting business continuity and authorized access scenarios.

name: Endpoint Detection and Response Tool
description: A security tool deployed across all endpoints to detect, monitor, and respond to suspicious behavior and malware threats in real-time.
context: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tool deployed

name: Antivirus and Anti-malware Scanning
description: A continuous monitoring control that performs real-time scanning of endpoint activity and maintains current virus definitions updated daily to detect and isolate malicious code.

name: Full-Disk Encryption
description: A mandatory encryption control implemented via BitLocker on Windows devices and FileVault on Mac devices, with encryption keys escrowed for recovery purposes. Required for all devices with access to customer data.
context: Mandatory for all devices with customer data access

name: Mobile Device Management System
description: A centralized management platform for controlling and securing mobile devices (phones and tablets), enabling enforcement of security policies, remote wipe capabilities, and patch management.

name: Operating System Patch Management
description: A systematic control process for applying operating system security patches within defined timeframes: standard patches within 30 days and critical patches within 7 days.
context: OS patches applied within 30 days (critical within 7)

name: Malware and Suspicious Behavior
description: The risk of malware infection and suspicious endpoint behavior that could compromise system integrity and customer data. Addressed through EDR deployment, real-time scanning, and automatic isolation controls.
context: Endpoint detection and response (EDR) tool deployed

name: Unauthorized Device Access
description: The risk of unauthorized access to devices and customer data through device loss, theft, or compromise. Mitigated through encryption, MDM, and remote wipe capabilities.
context: Mandatory for all devices with customer data access

name: Unpatched System Vulnerabilities
description: The risk of exploitation of known security vulnerabilities in operating systems and applications. Addressed through a tiered patch management schedule with expedited timelines for critical patches.
context: OS patches applied within 30 days (critical within 7)

name: Data Breach Through Unencrypted Devices
description: The risk of customer data exposure if devices containing such data are not encrypted. Mitigated through mandatory full-disk encryption with key escrow for all devices with customer data access.
context: Mandatory for all devices with customer data access

name: Application Security Policy
description: Policy governing secure software development lifecycle (SDLC) practices, including code review requirements, testing protocols, and deployment controls to prevent security vulnerabilities in production systems.

name: Peer Code Review Before Deployment
description: Mandatory requirement that all code must undergo peer review prior to deployment to production systems.

name: Security-Focused Code Review Checklist
description: Requirement to apply a security-focused code review checklist during the peer review process to identify potential security flaws.

name: Authorization Controls Review
description: Requirement to review authorization controls as part of the code review process to ensure proper access management is implemented.

name: SQL Injection and XSS Prevention Checks
description: Requirement to perform checks during code review to verify prevention of SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities.

name: Unit Testing by Developers
description: Requirement for developers to conduct unit testing as part of the development and testing process.

name: Integration Testing by QA
description: Requirement for QA teams to perform integration testing to verify that system components work together correctly.

name: Security Testing Including Penetration Tests and Vulnerability Scans
description: Requirement to conduct security testing including penetration tests and vulnerability scans to identify and remediate security weaknesses.

name: Load Testing Before Production Release
description: Requirement to perform load testing prior to releasing applications to production to ensure system performance and stability.

name: Automated Deployment Without Manual Production Changes
description: Prohibition on manual changes to production systems; all deployments must be automated to reduce human error and maintain audit trails.

name: Change Advisory Board Approval for Production Changes
description: Requirement that all changes to production systems must receive approval from the Change Advisory Board before deployment.
context: Change advisory board approval (changes to prod)

name: Documented Rollback Plan
description: Requirement to document a rollback plan for each deployment to enable rapid recovery in case of deployment failure or issues.

name: Production Monitoring Enablement
description: Requirement to enable monitoring of production systems to detect and respond to operational issues and security incidents.

name: Peer Code Review Process
description: Control mechanism requiring peer review of code before deployment, incorporating security-focused checklists and authorization controls review.

name: Penetration Testing and Vulnerability Scanning
description: Security testing control measure to identify vulnerabilities through penetration tests and automated vulnerability scans.

name: Automated Deployment System
description: Automated deployment mechanism that eliminates manual production changes and ensures consistent, auditable deployment processes.

name: Production Monitoring System
description: Monitoring system enabled on production environments to track system performance, detect anomalies, and support incident response.

name: Developer
description: Developers are responsible for conducting unit testing and participating in peer code reviews before deployment.

name: QA Team
description: QA teams are responsible for performing integration testing and security testing including penetration tests and vulnerability scans.

name: Change Advisory Board
description: The Change Advisory Board is responsible for approving all changes to production systems before deployment.
context: Change advisory board approval (changes to prod)

name: SQL Injection Vulnerability
description: Security risk of SQL injection attacks that could allow unauthorized database access or manipulation, addressed through code review prevention checks.

name: Cross-Site Scripting Vulnerability
description: Security risk of cross-site scripting attacks that could compromise user sessions or data, addressed through code review prevention checks.

name: Unauthorized Access Risk
description: Risk of unauthorized access to systems or data due to inadequate authorization controls, mitigated through authorization controls review.

name: Production System Failure
description: Operational risk of production system failures due to inadequate testing or deployment issues, mitigated through load testing and rollback planning.

name: Undetected Security Vulnerabilities
description: Risk of deploying applications with undetected security vulnerabilities, mitigated through security testing including penetration tests and vulnerability scans.

name: API Security Policy
description: Policy governing the security of API infrastructure and design, including authentication, rate limiting, request validation, input sanitization, output encoding, authorization checks, and audit logging requirements.

name: API Gateway Authentication
description: Authentication control mechanism implemented via API Gateway (Kong) using API key and JWT credentials to verify and authorize API access.

name: Rate Limiting
description: Control measure implemented at the API Gateway level to prevent abuse by limiting the rate of API requests from clients.

name: Request Validation
description: Control mechanism to prevent injection attacks by validating all incoming API requests at the gateway level.

name: API Monitoring and Alerting
description: Continuous monitoring and alerting system for API Gateway to detect and respond to security incidents and anomalies.

name: Input Validation and Sanitization
description: API design control requiring sanitization of all inputs to prevent injection attacks and malicious data processing.

name: Output Encoding
description: API design control to prevent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks by encoding all API output responses.

name: Role-Based Authorization Checks
description: API design control implementing role-based access control to ensure users can only access resources and operations appropriate to their assigned role.

name: API Call Audit Logging
description: Control measure requiring comprehensive audit logging of all API calls for compliance, security investigation, and operational monitoring purposes.

name: Injection Attack
description: Security risk addressed by request validation and input sanitization controls to prevent malicious code injection through API requests.

name: Cross-Site Scripting
description: Security risk mitigated through output encoding controls to prevent malicious scripts from being executed in API responses.

name: API Abuse
description: Risk of excessive or malicious API requests addressed through rate limiting controls at the API Gateway.

name: Unauthorized Access
description: Risk of unauthorized API access mitigated through authentication, authorization checks, and role-based access controls.

name: Vulnerability Management Policy
description: Policy governing the identification, assessment, and remediation of security vulnerabilities across production systems, pre-deployment environments, and third-party dependencies. Establishes scanning frequencies and mandates use of specific vulnerability assessment tools.

name: Production System Vulnerability Scanning
description: Mandatory requirement to perform vulnerability scans on production systems on a weekly basis to identify and assess security exposures in live environments.

name: Pre-Deployment Vulnerability Scanning
description: Mandatory requirement to conduct vulnerability scans prior to every release to ensure code and configurations are assessed before deployment to production.

name: Third-Party Library Continuous Scanning
description: Mandatory requirement to perform continuous scanning of third-party libraries and dependencies to detect vulnerabilities in external code components on an ongoing basis.

name: Network Vulnerability Scanner
description: Nessus network vulnerability scanner tool mandated for identifying security weaknesses and misconfigurations in network infrastructure and systems.

name: Web Application Scanner
description: Burp Suite web application scanner tool mandated for identifying vulnerabilities in web applications and APIs during security assessments.

name: Container Image Scanner
description: Trivy container image scanner tool mandated for scanning container images to identify vulnerabilities in containerized applications and their dependencies.

name: Dependency Checker
description: Dependency checking tools such as npm audit mandated for identifying known vulnerabilities in project dependencies and third-party libraries.

name: Information Security Risk
description: Security vulnerabilities in production systems, pre-deployment code, and third-party dependencies that could be exploited to compromise system integrity, confidentiality, or availability.

name: Patch Management Policy
description: Policy governing the identification, testing, and deployment of security patches across the organisation's IT infrastructure. Establishes criticality-based timelines for patch application and defines the end-to-end process from vulnerability identification through production verification.

name: Critical Patch Deployment Timeline
description: Mandatory requirement to deploy patches classified as Critical within 7 days of vendor release. This is the most stringent timeline reflecting the highest security risk.

name: High Priority Patch Deployment Timeline
description: Mandatory requirement to deploy patches classified as High priority within 30 days of vendor release.

name: Medium Priority Patch Deployment Timeline
description: Mandatory requirement to deploy patches classified as Medium priority within 60 days of vendor release.

name: Low Priority Patch Deployment Timeline
description: Mandatory requirement to deploy patches classified as Low priority within 90 days of vendor release.

name: Non-Production Testing Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement to test all patches in non-production environments prior to production deployment to ensure compatibility and stability.

name: Post-Deployment Verification and Monitoring
description: Mandatory requirement to verify patch deployment success and conduct ongoing monitoring in production environments following deployment.

name: Vulnerability Identification Process
description: Operational control mechanism for identifying security vulnerabilities that require patching. Serves as the initial trigger in the patch management workflow.

name: Vendor Patch Release Monitoring
description: Control mechanism for tracking and documenting when vendors release security patches, establishing the baseline date for criticality timeline calculations.

name: Non-Production Testing Environment
description: Operational safeguard requiring patches to be tested in isolated non-production environments before production deployment to validate functionality and prevent system disruption.

name: Production Deployment Verification
description: Control mechanism for verifying successful patch deployment in production and establishing ongoing monitoring to detect any adverse effects or deployment failures.

name: Security Vulnerability Risk
description: The risk of unpatched security vulnerabilities in IT systems that could be exploited by threat actors to compromise system integrity, confidentiality, or availability. The patch management policy is designed to mitigate this risk through timely remediation.

name: Third-Party Risk Management Policy
description: Policy governing the security assessment and ongoing monitoring of third-party vendors and service providers. Establishes pre-assessment requirements including security questionnaires, SOC 2 Type II audits, and penetration testing, along with continuous oversight mechanisms including annual re-assessments and incident notification protocols.

name: Security Questionnaire Completion
description: Vendors must complete a security questionnaire as part of the pre-assessment phase before engagement.

name: SOC 2 Type II Audit Review
description: FirstUK Bank must review SOC 2 Type II audit results from vendors when available as part of pre-assessment security evaluation.
context: SOC 2 Type II audit reviewed (if available)

name: Penetration Test Results Review
description: Penetration test results must be reviewed during pre-assessment when applicable to the vendor's service scope.

name: Vendor Reference Checks
description: Reference checks with other customers of the vendor must be conducted as part of the pre-assessment phase.

name: Annual Vendor Re-Assessment
description: Vendors must undergo annual re-assessment to ensure continued compliance with security standards and policy requirements.

name: Incident Notification Requirement
description: Vendors are required to notify FirstUK Bank of security incidents within 24 hours as defined by the Service Level Agreement.

name: Bank Audit Rights Over Vendor
description: FirstUK Bank retains the right to audit vendors to verify compliance with security and operational standards.
context: Audit rights (FirstUK Bank can audit vendor)

name: Service Level Agreement for Security
description: A Service Level Agreement must be established with vendors defining security performance standards and incident response obligations.

name: Security Questionnaire
description: Assessment tool used to gather security information from vendors during the pre-engagement phase.

name: SOC 2 Type II Audit Review
description: Review of SOC 2 Type II audit reports to verify vendor compliance with security and operational controls.
context: SOC 2 Type II audit reviewed (if available)

name: Penetration Testing
description: Security testing conducted by or for vendors to identify vulnerabilities in systems and infrastructure.

name: Vendor Reference Checks
description: Due diligence process involving consultation with other customers to assess vendor reliability and security practices.

name: Annual Vendor Security Re-Assessment
description: Periodic review and re-evaluation of vendor security posture and compliance status on an annual basis.

name: Incident Notification Monitoring
description: Monitoring mechanism to track vendor incident notifications and ensure compliance with the 24-hour SLA requirement.

name: Vendor Audit Program
description: FirstUK Bank's audit function to verify vendor compliance with contractual security obligations and policy requirements.
context: Audit rights (FirstUK Bank can audit vendor)

name: Third-Party Security Risk
description: Risk arising from security vulnerabilities, inadequate controls, or non-compliance by third-party vendors and service providers that could impact FirstUK Bank's operations, data, or reputation.

name: Vendor Incident Risk
description: Risk of security incidents occurring at vendor facilities or systems that could affect FirstUK Bank's services or customer data.

name: Third-Party Risk Manager
description: Role responsible for overseeing vendor security assessments, conducting pre-assessments, managing ongoing monitoring, and exercising audit rights over third-party vendors.
context: Audit rights (FirstUK Bank can audit vendor)

name: Third-Party Access Policy
description: Policy governing access by contractors and vendors to bank systems, establishing principles of least privilege, time-bound access, continuous monitoring, and mandatory security agreements. The policy mandates multi-factor authentication and automatic revocation of access rights.
context: Contractor/Vendor Access: Limited to systems needed, Time-bound (auto-revocation), Monitored (all actions logged), MFA required, NDA and security agreement signed

name: Contractor and Vendor System Access Limitation
description: Requirement that contractor and vendor access to bank systems be restricted to only those systems necessary for their contracted work, implementing the principle of least privilege.

name: Time-Bound Access with Automatic Revocation
description: Requirement that all third-party access grants be time-limited with automatic revocation upon expiry, preventing indefinite or orphaned access rights.

name: Comprehensive Logging of Third-Party Actions
description: Requirement that all actions performed by contractors and vendors on bank systems be logged and monitored to enable audit trails and detection of unauthorized or suspicious activity.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication for Third-Party Access
description: Requirement that all contractors and vendors must authenticate using multi-factor authentication when accessing bank systems, strengthening access controls beyond single-factor credentials.

name: Non-Disclosure Agreement and Security Agreement Execution
description: Requirement that contractors and vendors must execute both a Non-Disclosure Agreement and a security agreement prior to being granted access to bank systems, establishing legal and contractual obligations.

name: Access Control Limitation
description: Operational control restricting third-party system access to only those systems required for contracted duties, implementing least-privilege principles.

name: Automatic Access Revocation
description: Technical control mechanism that automatically terminates third-party access rights upon expiry of the time-bound access grant, preventing access persistence beyond authorized periods.

name: Audit Logging of Third-Party Actions
description: Monitoring and logging control that records all actions performed by contractors and vendors on bank systems, enabling forensic review and compliance verification.

name: Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Authentication control requiring contractors and vendors to use multiple authentication factors when accessing bank systems, reducing the risk of unauthorized access through credential compromise.

name: Third-Party Access Administrator
description: Role responsible for managing, monitoring, and enforcing third-party access controls, including provisioning, time-bound grants, and revocation of contractor and vendor system access.
context: Contractor/Vendor Access: Limited to systems needed, Time-bound (auto-revocation), Monitored (all actions logged)

name: Unauthorized Access
description: Risk that contractors or vendors may gain access to systems beyond their contracted scope or retain access after engagement termination, potentially enabling data theft, fraud, or system compromise.

name: Undetected Malicious Activity by Third Parties
description: Risk that contractors or vendors may perform unauthorized or malicious actions on bank systems without detection, compromising data integrity or system availability.

name: Credential Compromise of Third-Party Users
description: Risk that contractor or vendor credentials may be compromised, allowing unauthorized actors to impersonate legitimate third-party users and access bank systems.

name: Physical Security Policy
description: Policy governing physical security measures for data centers, including access control, environmental protection, and monitoring requirements to safeguard banking infrastructure and customer data.

name: Badge Access Control Requirement
description: Mandatory requirement that data center access be restricted to badge access only, with biometric authentication required at the main entrance.
context: Badge access only (biometric at main entrance)

name: Visitor Log Maintenance
description: Requirement to maintain a visitor log for all individuals entering the data center facility.

name: Escort Requirement for Non-Staff
description: Mandatory requirement that non-staff visitors must be escorted while present in the data center.

name: Continuous CCTV Monitoring
description: Requirement for 24/7 CCTV monitoring of data center facilities to detect and record unauthorized access or security incidents.

name: Fire Suppression System Installation
description: Requirement to maintain fire suppression systems, specifically sprinkler systems, in data center facilities.

name: Power Backup System Maintenance
description: Requirement to maintain power backup systems including generators and uninterruptible power supplies (UPS) to ensure continuous data center operations.

name: Climate Control System Operation
description: Requirement to maintain climate control systems that regulate temperature and humidity within data center facilities.

name: Water Detection System Installation
description: Requirement to install water detection systems to prevent flooding and water damage to data center infrastructure.

name: Badge Access Control System
description: Technical access control mechanism using badge-based authentication with biometric verification at the main entrance to restrict unauthorized physical access to data centers.
context: Badge access only (biometric at main entrance)

name: Visitor Logging System
description: Operational control mechanism for recording and tracking all visitor access to data center facilities.

name: CCTV Surveillance System
description: Continuous video surveillance system operating 24 hours per day, 7 days per week to monitor and record all activities within data center facilities.

name: Fire Suppression System
description: Environmental protection control using sprinkler-based fire suppression to prevent fire damage to data center infrastructure and equipment.

name: Power Backup System
description: Redundant power supply system comprising generators and uninterruptible power supplies to maintain continuous data center operations during power outages.

name: Climate Control System
description: Environmental control system that maintains optimal temperature and humidity levels within data center facilities to protect equipment and ensure operational efficiency.

name: Water Detection System
description: Environmental monitoring system designed to detect water intrusion and prevent flooding damage to data center infrastructure.

name: Unauthorized Physical Access
description: Risk of unauthorized individuals gaining physical access to data center facilities, potentially compromising banking infrastructure and customer data security.

name: Fire Damage
description: Risk of fire damage to data center facilities and equipment, potentially causing loss of banking services and customer data.

name: Power Failure
description: Risk of power outages causing interruption to data center operations and banking services.

name: Environmental Damage
description: Risk of environmental factors including temperature fluctuations, humidity extremes, and water intrusion causing damage to data center equipment and infrastructure.

name: Information Security Policy
description: Policy governing physical and information security controls at bank offices and branches, including access control, visitor management, and screen privacy measures to prevent unauthorized access and data exposure.
context: Privacy filters on laptops (when public spaces)

name: Badge Access Control
description: Physical access control mechanism requiring badge authentication for entry to offices and branches, with doors locked after hours to restrict unauthorized access.

name: Visitor Sign-In
description: Mandatory visitor registration and sign-in procedure to track and monitor non-employee access to bank premises.

name: Conference Room Locking
description: Physical security measure requiring conference rooms to be lockable to prevent unauthorized access to sensitive discussions and materials.

name: Secure Document Storage
description: Designated secure storage areas for sensitive documents to prevent unauthorized access and ensure proper document handling.

name: Desk Positioning for Privacy
description: Physical desk arrangement control to prevent shoulder-surfing and unauthorized viewing of sensitive information on employee screens.

name: Laptop Privacy Filter
description: Privacy filter technology deployed on laptops used in public spaces to restrict viewing angles and prevent unauthorized screen visibility.
context: Privacy filters on laptops (when public spaces)

name: Automatic Screen Lock
description: Automatic screen locking mechanism that engages after 15 minutes of inactivity to prevent unauthorized access to unattended workstations.

name: Information Security Risk
description: Risk of unauthorized access to sensitive customer and bank information through physical intrusion, shoulder-surfing, or unattended workstations.
context: Privacy filters on laptops (when public spaces)

name: Incident Response Policy
description: Policy governing the detection, reporting, classification, and escalation of security incidents within the organization. Defines immediate actions required upon incident detection and establishes a four-tier severity classification system ranging from critical data breaches to low-level policy violations.
context: Detect incident (automated alerts or staff report)
Escalate to CTO and CRO if confirmed

name: Incident Detection and Reporting Obligation
description: Requires staff and automated systems to detect incidents and report them to the Information Security Officer. Establishes the first critical step in the incident response process.
context: Detect incident (automated alerts or staff report)

name: Incident Escalation to Executive Leadership
description: Mandates escalation of confirmed incidents to the Chief Technology Officer and Chief Risk Officer. Ensures senior leadership visibility and decision-making authority for significant security events.
context: Escalate to CTO and CRO if confirmed

name: Incident Response Team Activation
description: Requires activation of the incident response team upon confirmed incident detection. Establishes the operational mechanism for coordinated incident management.

name: Incident Severity Classification
description: Establishes a four-tier severity classification system for incidents ranging from critical (Severity 1) to low (Severity 4). Provides clear criteria for categorizing incidents based on impact and nature of compromise.
context: Severity 1 (Critical): Data breach, ransomware, system unavailable
Severity 2 (High): Suspected breach, unauthorized access, significant compromise
Severity 3 (Medium): Malware detected, vulnerability found, access attempt
Severity 4 (Low): Policy violation, minor vulnerability, suspicious activity

name: Data Breach
description: Unauthorized disclosure or loss of sensitive customer or organizational data. Classified as Severity 1 (Critical) incident requiring immediate escalation and response team activation.
context: Severity 1 (Critical): Data breach, ransomware, system unavailable

name: Ransomware Attack
description: Malicious software that encrypts or locks organizational systems and data, typically demanding payment for restoration. Classified as Severity 1 (Critical) incident.
context: Severity 1 (Critical): Data breach, ransomware, system unavailable

name: System Unavailability
description: Loss of availability or functionality of critical systems preventing normal business operations. Classified as Severity 1 (Critical) incident.
context: Severity 1 (Critical): Data breach, ransomware, system unavailable

name: Suspected Data Breach
description: Unconfirmed indication of unauthorized data access or disclosure. Classified as Severity 2 (High) incident requiring escalation.
context: Severity 2 (High): Suspected breach, unauthorized access, significant compromise

name: Unauthorized Access
description: Unapproved access to systems, data, or resources by internal or external actors. Classified as Severity 2 (High) incident.
context: Severity 2 (High): Suspected breach, unauthorized access, significant compromise

name: Significant System Compromise
description: Material degradation or partial loss of system integrity, confidentiality, or availability. Classified as Severity 2 (High) incident.
context: Severity 2 (High): Suspected breach, unauthorized access, significant compromise

name: Malware Detection
description: Discovery of malicious software on organizational systems. Classified as Severity 3 (Medium) incident.
context: Severity 3 (Medium): Malware detected, vulnerability found, access attempt

name: Vulnerability
description: Identified weakness or flaw in systems, applications, or processes that could be exploited. Classified as Severity 3 (Medium) incident.
context: Severity 3 (Medium): Malware detected, vulnerability found, access attempt

name: Access Attempt
description: Detected effort to gain unauthorized access to systems or data. Classified as Severity 3 (Medium) incident.
context: Severity 3 (Medium): Malware detected, vulnerability found, access attempt

name: Policy Violation
description: Non-compliance with organizational security or operational policies. Classified as Severity 4 (Low) incident.
context: Severity 4 (Low): Policy violation, minor vulnerability, suspicious activity

name: Minor Vulnerability
description: Low-impact security weakness with limited exploitation potential. Classified as Severity 4 (Low) incident.
context: Severity 4 (Low): Policy violation, minor vulnerability, suspicious activity

name: Suspicious Activity
description: Unusual or potentially malicious behavior detected on systems or accounts. Classified as Severity 4 (Low) incident.
context: Severity 4 (Low): Policy violation, minor vulnerability, suspicious activity

name: Automated Incident Detection
description: Automated monitoring and alerting system that detects security incidents without manual intervention. Serves as the primary detection mechanism for incident response.
context: Detect incident (automated alerts or staff report)

name: Staff Incident Reporting
description: Manual reporting mechanism enabling staff to report detected or suspected incidents. Complements automated detection systems.
context: Detect incident (automated alerts or staff report)

name: Information Security Officer
description: Role responsible for receiving initial incident reports and determining whether escalation to executive leadership is warranted. Serves as the first point of contact for incident reporting.

name: Chief Technology Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving escalation of confirmed incidents and providing technical leadership in incident response.
context: Escalate to CTO and CRO if confirmed

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive role responsible for receiving escalation of confirmed incidents and providing risk management oversight in incident response.
context: Escalate to CTO and CRO if confirmed

name: Incident Response Team
description: Cross-functional team activated upon confirmed incident detection to coordinate investigation, containment, and remediation activities.

name: Incident Investigation Policy
description: Policy governing the investigation of security incidents and operational failures, with severity-based response timelines and mandatory investigation elements. Defines the procedural framework for determining incident scope, root cause, data impact, and customer exposure.

name: Severity 1 Incident Investigation Initiation
description: Requires that Severity 1 incidents trigger immediate investigation commencement without delay.

name: Severity 2 Incident Investigation Initiation
description: Requires that Severity 2 incidents must have investigation commenced within 2 hours of detection or notification.

name: Severity 3 Incident Investigation Initiation
description: Requires that Severity 3 incidents must have investigation commenced within 24 hours of detection or notification.

name: Severity 4 Incident Investigation Initiation
description: Requires that Severity 4 incidents must have investigation commenced within 1 week of detection or notification.

name: Incident Timeline Documentation
description: Requires investigation to document and establish the complete timeline of what happened during the incident.

name: Root Cause Analysis
description: Requires investigation to determine and document how the incident occurred, including identification of root cause.

name: Data Impact Assessment
description: Requires investigation to identify and document what data was affected or compromised by the incident.

name: Customer Impact Quantification
description: Requires investigation to determine and document the number of customers impacted by the incident.

name: Compromise Extent Assessment
description: Requires investigation to assess and document the full extent of compromise resulting from the incident.

name: Operational Risk
description: Operational risks and failures that trigger incident investigation procedures, including system failures, security breaches, and other operational incidents classified by severity level.

name: Data Breach
description: Risk of unauthorized access to or compromise of customer data, which is a key investigation element requiring assessment of affected data and customer impact.

name: Incident Containment and Recovery Policy
description: Policy governing the containment and recovery procedures for information security incidents, including isolation of affected systems, evidence preservation, malware quarantine, backup restoration, vulnerability patching, and integrity verification.
context: Restore affected systems from clean backup

name: System Isolation on Security Incident
description: Requirement to immediately isolate affected systems by disconnecting them from the network upon detection of a security incident.

name: Evidence Preservation During Incident Response
description: Obligation to preserve all forensic evidence including logs, memory dumps, and disk contents during incident containment to support investigation and recovery.

name: Malware Quarantine and Spread Prevention
description: Requirement to quarantine malware and prevent its spread to other systems as part of the containment phase.

name: Backup Restoration from Uncompromised Source
description: Provision to restore affected systems from clean, uncompromised backup copies as part of the recovery process.
context: Restore affected systems from clean backup

name: Vulnerability Patching Post-Incident
description: Obligation to patch the vulnerability that enabled the security incident as part of the recovery phase.

name: Post-Recovery System Integrity Verification
description: Requirement to verify the integrity of systems following restoration from backup to ensure complete recovery and absence of residual compromise.

name: Gradual Production Restoration
description: Requirement to restore affected systems to production gradually rather than immediately, allowing for monitoring and validation.

name: Information Security Incident
description: Risk category encompassing unauthorized access, malware infection, data breach, or other compromise of information systems requiring containment and recovery procedures.

name: System Isolation Control
description: Operational control requiring immediate disconnection of affected systems from the network to prevent further compromise or spread of incidents.

name: Forensic Evidence Preservation
description: Control measure requiring preservation of logs, memory dumps, and disk contents to support forensic investigation and incident analysis.

name: Malware Quarantine System
description: Protective mechanism to isolate and contain malware, preventing its propagation to other systems during incident response.

name: Backup and Restore Capability
